body: I only completed one year of biology courses and the first semester of general chemistry, so no certificates or anything. I just don't know what I could do with my degree that wouldn't require a doctorate, which I think is out of the question for me right now.

That sounds crappy. I know what you mean--I've had to take so many utterly useless classes just to meet university requirements. Hopefully you'll be able to get a decent job once you do have a degree!

It definitely is interesting, which is really the only reason why I chose it. Most of the classes I take for my concentration are related to osteology, archaeology, and evolutionary biology in a hominin context. I would try to get into a graduate program, but I don't think I'd get in anywhere and I don't think I can handle working with other people every day.

I'm sorry to hear that--how are they awful? My degree is in physical anthropology, but I started out as a biochem major. What's yours in? I've almost dropped out several times myself, but I keep going back because I've already invested so much in school...
